Melbourne and the regions

Event Planners in Melbourne

Melbourne plans on a compact map under an unreliable sky. The Yarra Valley and the Mornington Peninsula are both about an hour out, and one afternoon in October can hand you a heat plan and a wet weather plan at once. Tell us what you are building and we will pass the brief on.

No cost to enquireYou choose whether to book, and you pay the planner directly.
Get event planning quotesHow planning works
  • An hour to wine countryThe Yarra Valley and the Peninsula are day trips, not expeditions.
  • Two weather plansA heat call and a wet call can share one month.
  • Dry hire is commonPower, furniture and catering all arrive on a truck.

Decide the wet weather plan in month one, not on the morning.

Melbourne can deliver thirty eight degrees and a cold change in the same week, so a covered structure either sits in the budget from the start or the site has a real indoor option. There is no third answer.

This city holds an unusual amount of empty space. Warehouses through Collingwood, Abbotsford and Cremorne, studios in the inner north, laneway rooms behind the CBD: all of them hired as four walls and a key. That is why event planners in Melbourne spend more of the first meeting on logistics than on styling. Power, furniture, kitchen access, bar equipment, staffing and waste are yours to solve in a dry hire space, and they are the reason a cheap room can need more planning hours than an expensive one.

The calendar does the rest. Spring racing and the football finals compress venue and crew availability through October and November, June runs hard on the financial year, and the two regions this city celebrates in, the Yarra Valley and the Mornington Peninsula, sit about an hour beyond the tram network. Send one brief and let planners answer it. Melbourne businesses answer to both event planning and event management, and the distinction is a marketing one rather than a real one. Event management Melbourne enquiries land with the same planners.

In and around Melbourne

What are you planning in Melbourne?

What people hand over here, and where the local difficulty actually sits in each one. Every card links to the national page that explains the service in full.

Start with

Weddings

Two thirds of the conversation is weather and licence. A planner sets the hour the wet call is made and names the person making it, then reads the venue's curfew, because in Melbourne the licence decides more of the run sheet than the couple does.

Find planners

Parties and milestones

Parties run right through winter, so a great deal of this work is indoor: heating, coat storage and a room that holds up when nobody wants to step outside. In Fitzroy, Richmond and Prahran the practical limits are the loading zone window and the hour the music has to stop.

Find planners

Corporate events

Conferences, launches, awards and staff nights, quoted against a written brief and an approval chain that needs a paper trail. In the CBD and Southbank the dock and the lift set the bump in; in a Collingwood warehouse there is no dock at all.

Find planners

Engagement parties

Usually six to twelve weeks of notice and a room rather than a build. Small function spaces through Carlton, South Yarra and St Kilda take most of them, and the help worth paying for is a supplier shortlist plus somebody running the night.

Find planners

Proposals

A proposal in a public place is a council question here as much as a romantic one. Street occupancy, amplified sound and anything built on a footpath each carry their own approval, and lead times differ by council, so the paperwork starts weeks before the moment does.

Find planners

Private celebrations

Christenings, wakes, anniversaries, a fiftieth in a rented studio, a long lunch out on the Peninsula. Planners take them at the same three levels as anything else, and in a dry hire room the smallest of these still needs power, furniture and a bar plan.

Planning support

How much help do you want in Melbourne?

The same three levels sell under a dozen names, and naming yours is what makes two quotes comparable. In a dry hire space the level matters more than usual, because full planning here includes building the room itself.

Full planning

A planner carries the whole build with you, from the first budget conversation to the last supplier leaving.

Usually engaged nine to fourteen months out.

  • Budget built and tracked
  • Venue and supplier shortlists
  • Contracts and payment schedule
  • Run sheet and floor plan
  • On the day, start to finish

Partial planning

You have made a start. A planner picks up the parts that have stalled and brings the rest into one plan.

Often engaged four to eight months out.

  • Picks up from where you are
  • Fills the supplier gaps
  • Tidies the budget
  • Builds the run sheet
  • Hands back a plan you can follow

On-the-day coordination

Your plan is built. A coordinator takes it over in the final weeks and runs the day so you can be in it.

Usually engaged four to eight weeks out.

  • Reads and stress-tests your plan
  • Confirms every supplier
  • Owns the run sheet
  • First point of contact on the day
  • Handles what goes sideways

Venue sourcing

Planners who know a market can shortlist against your date, your numbers and your budget rather than sending you back to the same search results.

Event coordination

Coordination is the execution layer: suppliers confirmed, a run sheet everyone has, and one person answering questions on the day.

Wedding coordination

A wedding coordinator takes a plan you have already built and runs the day itself, so nobody in the wedding party is directing traffic.

Choosing well

Finding the right planner in Melbourne

Four questions that separate a good Melbourne quote from a cheap one. Each has a written answer, and each one is easier to ask now than to discover in the last fortnight.

No. 01

Ask what the venue does not include

Dry hire is the default across the inner north and inner west, and the word covers a wide range. Get a list: power distribution, kitchen access, furniture, bar equipment, glassware, staffing, cleaning and waste. A planner who has worked the building can tell you which of those the landlord supplies and which arrive on a truck.

No. 02

Get the weather plan in writing

Not a reassurance, a procedure: the hour the call is made, who makes it, where everyone moves to and how long the move takes. If the site has no covered alternative, the honest options are hiring a structure and carrying it in the budget from month one, or choosing a different site. Deciding on the morning does not work.

No. 03

Count the site visits to the valley

If your event is in the Yarra Valley or on the Mornington Peninsula, ask for the number of included visits in writing. At roughly an hour each way many planners absorb several without a travel charge, but the included count varies a great deal between quotes and every extra visit is priced on its own.

No. 04

Ask about the street, not just the room

Load in here often happens across a public footpath, sometimes on a tram route, sometimes with a bike lane between the kerb and the door. A loading zone on a tram route can be unusable during peak service. Ask where the truck stops, for how long, and what needs a council permit, then tell every supplier before they quote.

A warehouse can look cheap as a venue and still take more planning hours than a ballroom.

On the ground

Where a Melbourne plan usually bends

Three pressure points come up again and again in this city, and none of them appears on a mood board. Sort them early and the rest of the plan tends to hold.

Two seasons in one afternoon

Weather here is a scheduling problem rather than a seasonal one. A thirty eight degree day and a cold change can land in the same week in November, so a genuine plan names the decision hour, the person who owns the call and the covered space guests move into. Heat has its own consequences: a warehouse with no air conditioning is hard to work in, and a crew that has been loading since ten is measurably slower by five. Summer bump ins need a longer window and water on the crew plan.

An hour to the valley and the peninsula

Almost everything this city celebrates outside the tram network sits about an hour away. The Yarra Valley runs east, the Mornington Peninsula south, and both are close enough that suppliers generally treat them as a long day rather than an expedition. That keeps travel charges lower than they would be in a state with real distance, but it does not make them free. The number that matters in a quote is included site visits, because an hour each way turns one meeting into most of a working day.

Heritage rooms, laneways and permits

Older buildings across the CBD and Carlton bring load in restrictions that a modern venue does not have: narrow stairs, a lift with a weight limit, no dock, and a street that is shared with trams and pedestrians. Add council approvals on top.

  • Street occupancy for a footpath or laneway build
  • Amplified sound, assessed separately from the occupancy
  • Crane or hoist access where the stairs will not take it
  • Curfews written into the venue licence, not the contract

Final preparations, the hour before doors

Questions

Planning an event in Melbourne

How much does an event planner cost in Melbourne?

Less than Sydney, on the only guide that breaks the figure down by city. Airtasker's Australian cost guide, updated February 2025, gives Melbourne a median of $1,800 to $2,200, which sits closer to coordination than to full planning, so read it as a floor rather than an average for a full build. What moves the number here is dry hire: a shell venue adds power, furniture, catering facilities and staffing to the planner's scope, and the hours follow.

What does dry hire mean, and why does it cost more to plan?

Dry hire means the venue supplies the space and very little else. Power distribution, furniture, kitchen access, bar equipment, glassware, staffing and waste all become part of your plan, which is why an inner Melbourne warehouse can look cheap as a venue and still need more planning hours than a packaged function centre. Ask for the inclusion list in writing before you compare a shell against a room with catering built in.

Our Melbourne venue has no indoor alternative. What should we do?

Treat it as a booking decision rather than a weather one. Either a covered structure is hired and carried in the budget from the start, or you choose a site with a genuine indoor option at the same address. Melbourne can produce a heat day and a cold change in the same fortnight, so leaving the call to the morning gives you no supplier availability and no time. Whichever way you go, the decision belongs in month one.

Does the spring racing and finals period affect availability?

Yes, and it stacks with the pre-Christmas run. From late October through mid December the inner city is at its tightest, and the shortage is crew rather than rooms: audio visual technicians, wait staff and security commit before the venues fill. June is the other pressure point, driven by the financial year. If your date sits in either window, confirm suppliers rather than pencilling them.

Can a planner handle council permits for a Melbourne street or park event?

A planner will normally prepare the application, lodge it and manage the conditions attached, but the council decides and the timeframe is theirs. Melbourne councils differ on lead times and on what triggers a permit, and street occupancy, crane access and amplified sound are each assessed separately. None of them is a same week decision, so raise the site in the first conversation rather than after the venue is signed.

How many site visits should a Yarra Valley quote include?

Ask for the number in writing, because it varies more than the fee does. At about an hour from the city, many planners include several visits to the Yarra Valley or the Mornington Peninsula without charging travel, while others include one and price the rest individually. One visit consumes most of a working day, so the included count is often worth more than a small difference in the headline price.
